sentences.zh: 王顯，字世榮，陽平樂平人，自言本東海郯人，王朗之後也。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, courtesy name Shirong, was a man of Leping in Yangping; he himself said his origin was Tan in Donghai, descendant of Wang Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, courtesy name Shirong, was a native of Leping in Yangping; he himself said his origin was Tan in Donghai, descendant of Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 祖父延和中南奔，居于魯郊，又居彭城。

translations.literal: His grandfather in Yanhe fled south; he settled in the Lu suburbs, then lived in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather in Yanhe fled south; he settled in the Lu suburbs, then lived in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 伯父安上，劉義隆時板行館陶縣。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Anshang, in Liu Yilong's time was appointed Acting Magistrate of Guantao county.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Anshang, in Liu Yilong's time was appointed Acting Magistrate of Guantao county.

sentences.zh: 世祖南討，安上棄縣歸命，與父母俱徙平城，例敍陽都子，除廣寧太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu marched south, Anshang abandoned the county and submitted; with parents he was both moved to Pingcheng; by precedent enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangdu; removed as Administrator of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched south, Anshang abandoned the county and submitted; with parents he was both moved to Pingcheng; by precedent enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangdu; removed as Administrator of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 顯父安道，少與李亮同師，[14]俱學醫藥，粗究其術，而不及亮也。

translations.literal: Xian's father Andao in youth studied under the same teacher as Li Liang, [14] both learning medicine, roughly investigating the art but not reaching Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's father Andao in youth studied under the same teacher as Li Liang, [14] both learning medicine, roughly investigating the art but not reaching Liang.

sentences.zh: 安上還家樂平，頗參士流。

translations.literal: Anshang returned home to Leping, quite participating in the gentry stream.
translations.idiomatic: Anshang returned home to Leping, quite participating in the gentry stream.

sentences.zh: 顯少歷本州從事，雖以醫術自通，而明敏有決斷才用。

translations.literal: Xian in youth successively served as Attendant of this province; though making a profession of medical arts, he was bright, keen, and had decisive talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xian in youth successively served as Attendant of this province; though making a profession of medical arts, he was bright, keen, and had decisive talent.

sentences.zh: 初文昭皇太后之懷世宗也，夢為日所逐，化而為龍而繞后，后寤而驚悸，遂成心疾。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wen was pregnant with Emperor Shizong, she dreamed of being chased by the sun, transforming into a dragon that coiled around the empress; the empress awoke startled and fearful, and thus formed a heart illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wen was pregnant with Emperor Shizong, she dreamed of being chased by the sun, transforming into a dragon that coiled around the empress; the empress awoke startled and fearful, and thus formed a heart illness.

sentences.zh: 文明太后敕召徐謇及顯等為后診脉。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Xu Jian and Xian and others to feel the empress's pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Xu Jian and Xian and others to feel the empress's pulse.

sentences.zh: 謇云是微風入藏，宜進湯加針。

translations.literal: Jian said it was slight wind entering the viscera—suitable to advance decoction and add needles.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said it was slight wind entering the viscera—suitable to advance decoction and add needles.

sentences.zh: 顯云：「案三部脉非有心疾，將是懷孕生男之象。

translations.literal: Xian said, "Examining the three-part pulse, it is not heart illness—it should be the sign of pregnancy bearing a male.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Examining the three-part pulse, it is not heart illness—it should be the sign of pregnancy bearing a male.

sentences.zh: 」果如顯言。

translations.literal: " It happened exactly as Xian said.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened exactly as Xian said.

sentences.zh: 久之，召補侍御師、尚書儀曹郎，號稱幹事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Attending Physician and Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section of the Imperial Secretariat, called capable in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Attending Physician and Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section of the Imperial Secretariat, called capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗自幼有微疾，久未差愈，顯攝療有效，因是稍蒙眄識。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong from youth had a slight illness, long not fully recovered; Xian's treatment had effect, and for this he gradually received favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong from youth had a slight illness, long not fully recovered; Xian's treatment had effect, and for this he gradually received favor.

sentences.zh: 又罷六輔之初，顯為領軍于烈間通規策，頗有密功。

translations.literal: Also at the beginning of abolishing the Six Assistants, Xian through Commander Yu Lie communicated plans and stratagems, having considerable secret merit.
translations.idiomatic: Also at the beginning of abolishing the Six Assistants, Xian through Commander Yu Lie communicated plans and stratagems, having considerable secret merit.

sentences.zh: 累遷游擊將軍，拜廷尉少卿，仍在侍御，營進御藥，出入禁內。

translations.literal: He repeatedly rose to General Who Strikes Suddenly, appointed Vice Minister of Justice, still in attendance, managing imperial drugs, entering and leaving the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly rose to General Who Strikes Suddenly, appointed Vice Minister of Justice, still in attendance, managing imperial drugs, entering and leaving the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 乞臨本州，世宗曾許之，積年未授，因是聲問傳于遠近。

translations.literal: Begging to oversee his native province, Emperor Shizong once promised it; accumulated years without appointment—thus reports spread far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Begging to oversee his native province, Emperor Shizong once promised it; accumulated years without appointment—thus reports spread far and near.

sentences.zh: 顯每語人，言時旨已決，必為刺史。

translations.literal: Xian often told people that the time's intent was already decided—he would surely become governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xian often told people that the time's intent was already decided—he would surely become governor.

sentences.zh: 遂除平北將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was thereupon removed to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon removed to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋詔馳驛還京，復掌藥，又遣還州。

translations.literal: Soon an edict dispatched post-horses to return to the capital, again managing drugs, again sent back to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict dispatched post-horses to return to the capital, again managing drugs, again sent back to the province.

sentences.zh: 元愉作逆，顯討之不利。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu rebelled; Xian attacked but was unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu rebelled; Xian attacked but was unsuccessful.

sentences.zh: 入除太府卿、御史中尉。

translations.literal: Entering he was removed to Minister of the Grand Storehouse and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Entering he was removed to Minister of the Grand Storehouse and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 顯前後歷職，所在著稱，糾折庶獄，究其姦回，出內惜慎，憂國如家。

translations.literal: Xian in his successive posts was renowned where he was; correcting and breaking through various cases, investigating their treachery and deceit; going out and entering he was cautious, grieving for the state as for his own family.
translations.idiomatic: Xian in his successive posts was renowned where he was; correcting and breaking through various cases, investigating their treachery and deceit; going out and entering he was cautious, grieving for the state as for his own family.

sentences.zh: 及領憲臺，多所彈劾，百僚肅然。

translations.literal: When he headed the censorate he impeached many; the hundred officials were all reverent.
translations.idiomatic: When he headed the censorate he impeached many; the hundred officials were all reverent.

sentences.zh: 又以中尉屬官不悉稱職，諷求更換。

translations.literal: Also because censorate subordinate officials did not all fit their posts, he hinted at seeking replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Also because censorate subordinate officials did not all fit their posts, he hinted at seeking replacement.

sentences.zh: 詔委改選，務盡才能，而顯所舉或有請屬，未皆得人，於是眾口喧譁，聲望致損。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted reselection, striving to exhaust talent and ability—but those Xian recommended sometimes had requests and connections, not all obtaining the right men; thereupon public clamor, reputation damaged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict entrusted reselection, striving to exhaust talent and ability—but those Xian recommended sometimes had requests and connections, not all obtaining the right men; thereupon public clamor, reputation damaged.

sentences.zh: 後世宗詔顯撰藥方三十五卷，班布天下，以療諸疾。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shizong ordered Xian to compile thirty-five scrolls of medical formulas, distributed throughout the realm to treat various illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Shizong ordered Xian to compile thirty-five scrolls of medical formulas, distributed throughout the realm to treat various illnesses.

sentences.zh: 東宮既建，以為太子詹事，委任甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, entrusted very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, entrusted very generously.

sentences.zh: 世宗每幸東宮，顯常迎侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong each time visited the Eastern Palace, Xian always welcomed and attended.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong each time visited the Eastern Palace, Xian always welcomed and attended.

sentences.zh: 出入禁中，仍奉醫藥。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the forbidden precinct, he still attended with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Entering and leaving the forbidden precinct, he still attended with medicine.

sentences.zh: 賞賜累加，為立館宇，寵振當時。

translations.literal: Rewards repeatedly increased; a residence was built for him; favor shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards repeatedly increased; a residence was built for him; favor shook the age.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年秋，以營療之功，封衞南伯。

translations.literal: In the autumn of Yanchang 2, for merit in managing treatment, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Yanchang 2, for merit in managing treatment, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Weinan.

translations.literal: Collation note 15.
translations.idiomatic: Collation note 15.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，世宗夜崩，肅宗踐祚。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Emperor Shizong died suddenly at night; Emperor Suzong ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Emperor Shizong died suddenly at night; Emperor Suzong ascended.

sentences.zh: 顯參奉璽策，隨從臨哭，微為憂懼。

translations.literal: Xian participated in presenting the seal edict, followed in attending the mourning, slightly fearful and anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Xian participated in presenting the seal edict, followed in attending the mourning, slightly fearful and anxious.

sentences.zh: 顯既蒙任遇，兼為法官，恃勢使威，為時所疾。

translations.literal: Xian having received appointment and favor, also serving as judge, relied on power and wielded authority—hated by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xian having received appointment and favor, also serving as judge, relied on power and wielded authority—hated by the age.

sentences.zh: 朝宰託以侍療無效，執之禁中，詔削爵位。

translations.literal: Court ministers entrusted on the grounds that attendance in treatment was ineffective, seized him in the forbidden precinct; an edict stripped rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers entrusted on the grounds that attendance in treatment was ineffective, seized him in the forbidden precinct; an edict stripped rank and title.

sentences.zh: 臨執呼冤，直閤以刀鐶撞其腋下，傷中吐血，至右衞府一宿死。

translations.literal: At the time of seizure he cried injustice; a Direct Attendant struck his armpit with an iron ring, wounding the middle and spitting blood—one night at the Right Guard headquarters he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of seizure he cried injustice; a Direct Attendant struck his armpit with an iron ring, wounding the middle and spitting blood—one night at the Right Guard headquarters he died.

sentences.zh: 始顯布衣為諸生，有沙門相顯後當富貴，誡其勿為吏官，吏官必敗。

translations.literal: At the start when Xian was in plain clothes as a student, a monk physiognomized him and said he would later be rich and noble, admonishing him not to become an official—an official post would surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: At the start when Xian was in plain clothes as a student, a monk physiognomized him and said he would later be rich and noble, admonishing him not to become an official—an official post would surely fail.

sentences.zh: 由是世宗時或欲令其遂攝吏部，每殷勤避之。

translations.literal: For this in Emperor Shizong's time when they sometimes wished to have him directly oversee the Ministry of Personnel, each time he earnestly avoided it.
translations.idiomatic: For this in Emperor Shizong's time when they sometimes wished to have him directly oversee the Ministry of Personnel, each time he earnestly avoided it.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，肅宗夜即位，受璽冊，於儀須兼太尉及吏部，倉卒百官不具，以顯兼吏部行事矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Emperor Suzong at night ascended, received the seal register; in the rites one must concurrently be Grand Commandant and Ministry of Personnel—hurriedly the hundred officials were not complete—Xian acted concurrently for the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong died, Emperor Suzong at night ascended, received the seal register; in the rites one must concurrently be Grand Commandant and Ministry of Personnel—hurriedly the hundred officials were not complete—Xian acted concurrently for the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 崔彧，字文若，清河東武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Yu, courtesy name Wenruo, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu, courtesy name Wenruo, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父勳之，字寧國，位大司馬外兵郎，贈通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Xunzhi, courtesy name Ningguo, held the post of Outer Section Officer of the Grand Marshal, posthumously granted Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xunzhi, courtesy name Ningguo, held the post of Outer Section Officer of the Grand Marshal, posthumously granted Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彧與兄相如俱自南入國。

translations.literal: Yu and his elder brother Xiangru both from the south entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and his elder brother Xiangru both from the south entered the state.

sentences.zh: 相如以才學知名，早卒。

translations.literal: Xiangru was known for talent and learning; he died early.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru was known for talent and learning; he died early.

sentences.zh: 彧少嘗詣青州，逢隱逸沙門，教以素問九卷及甲乙，遂善醫術。

translations.literal: Yu in youth once went to Qingzhou; he met a reclusive monk who taught him the nine scrolls of the Plain Questions and the A and B [canons], and thus became skilled at medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu in youth once went to Qingzhou; he met a reclusive monk who taught him the nine scrolls of the Plain Questions and the A and B [canons], and thus became skilled at medical arts.

sentences.zh: 中山王英子略曾病，王顯等不能療，彧針之，抽針即愈。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying's son Lüe once fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not treat him; Yu needled him—when the needle was withdrawn he immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying's son Lüe once fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not treat him; Yu needled him—when the needle was withdrawn he immediately recovered.

sentences.zh: 後位冀州別駕，累遷寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Aide-de-Camp of Jizhou; repeatedly rose to General of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held the post of Aide-de-Camp of Jizhou; repeatedly rose to General of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 性仁恕，見疾苦，好與治之。

translations.literal: By nature benevolent and forgiving; seeing suffering and illness, he liked to treat them.
translations.idiomatic: By nature benevolent and forgiving; seeing suffering and illness, he liked to treat them.

sentences.zh: 廣教門生，令多救療。

translations.literal: He broadly taught disciples, ordering many to save and treat.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly taught disciples, ordering many to save and treat.

sentences.zh: 其弟子清河趙約、勃海郝文法之徒咸亦有名。

translations.literal: His disciples Zhao Yue of Qinghe, Hao Wenfa of Bohai, and others were also famous.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Zhao Yue of Qinghe, Hao Wenfa of Bohai, and others were also famous.

sentences.zh: 彧子景哲，豪率，亦以醫術知名。

translations.literal: Yu's son Jingzhe, bold and unrestrained, was also known for medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Jingzhe, bold and unrestrained, was also known for medical arts.

sentences.zh: 為太中大夫、司徒長史。

translations.literal: He was Grand Master of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Master of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 蔣少游，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shaoyou was a man of Bochang in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shaoyou was a native of Bochang in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜之平東陽，見俘入於平城，充平齊戶，後配雲中為兵。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao pacified Dongyang, he was seen as a captive and entered Pingcheng, assigned as a Pingqi household, later matched to Yunzhong as soldier.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao pacified Dongyang, he was seen as a captive and entered Pingcheng, assigned as a Pingqi household, later matched to Yunzhong as soldier.

sentences.zh: 性機巧，頗能畫刻。

translations.literal: By nature ingenious, he was quite able at painting and carving.
translations.idiomatic: By nature ingenious, he was quite able at painting and carving.

sentences.zh: 有文思，吟咏之際，時有短篇。

translations.literal: He had literary thought; in the intervals of chanting and reciting he sometimes had short pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary thought; in the intervals of chanting and reciting he sometimes had short pieces.

sentences.zh: 遂留寄平城，以傭寫書為業，而名猶在鎮。

translations.literal: He then remained lodged at Pingcheng, taking copying books as profession, yet his name was still at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He then remained lodged at Pingcheng, taking copying books as profession, yet his name was still at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 後被召為中書寫書生，與高聰俱依高允。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as a copyist of the Central Secretariat, together with Gao Cong both relying on Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned as a copyist of the Central Secretariat, together with Gao Cong both relying on Gao Yun.

sentences.zh: 允愛其文用，遂並薦之，與聰俱補中書博士。

translations.literal: Yun loved his literary use, then both recommended them, and with Cong both were appointed Erudites of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yun loved his literary use, then both recommended them, and with Cong both were appointed Erudites of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自在中書，恒庇李沖兄弟子姪之門。

translations.literal: From being in the Central Secretariat he always sheltered the brothers, sons, and nephews of Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: From being in the Central Secretariat he always sheltered the brothers, sons, and nephews of Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 始北方不悉青州蔣族，或謂少游本非人士，又少游微因工藝自達，是以公私人望不至相重。

translations.literal: At first the north did not know the Jiang clan of Qingzhou; some said Shaoyou was originally not a gentry man, and Shaoyou slightly because of craftsmanship reached advancement—thus public and private repute did not reach mutual weight.
translations.idiomatic: At first the north did not know the Jiang clan of Qingzhou; some said Shaoyou was originally not a gentry man, and Shaoyou slightly because of craftsmanship reached advancement—thus public and private repute did not reach mutual weight.

sentences.zh: 唯高允、李沖曲為體練，由少游舅氏崔光與李沖從叔衍對門婚姻也。

translations.literal: Only Gao Yun and Li Chong bent to cultivate him bodily—because Shaoyou's maternal uncle Cui Guang and Li Chong's father's younger brother Yan were opposite-door marriage kin.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Yun and Li Chong bent to cultivate him bodily—because Shaoyou's maternal uncle Cui Guang and Li Chong's father's younger brother Yan were opposite-door marriage kin.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后常因密宴，謂百官曰：「本謂少游作師耳，高允老公乃言其人士。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming often at secret banquets told the hundred officials, "Originally I thought Shaoyou would be a teacher only; old man Gao Yun said he is a gentry man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming often at secret banquets told the hundred officials, "Originally I thought Shaoyou would be a teacher only; old man Gao Yun said he is a gentry man.

sentences.zh: 」眷識如此。

translations.literal: " Favor and recognition were like this.
translations.idiomatic: " Favor and recognition were like this.

sentences.zh: 然猶驟被引命，屑屑禁闥，以規矩刻繢為務，因此大蒙恩錫，超等備位，而亦不遷陟也。

translations.literal: Yet he was repeatedly summoned by order, busy in the forbidden gate, with compass, ruler, carving, and painting as his task—therefore greatly receiving grace and gifts, exceeding rank in filling posts, yet also not promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was repeatedly summoned by order, busy in the forbidden gate, with compass, ruler, carving, and painting as his task—therefore greatly receiving grace and gifts, exceeding rank in filling posts, yet also not promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 及詔尚書李沖與馮誕、游明根、高閭等議定衣冠於禁中，少游巧思，令主其事，亦訪於劉昶。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong together with Feng Dan, You Minggen, and Gao Lu to discuss robes and caps in the forbidden precinct, Shaoyou's clever thought ordered him to chiefly manage the affair; he also consulted Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong together with Feng Dan, You Minggen, and Gao Lu to discuss robes and caps in the forbidden precinct, Shaoyou's clever thought ordered him to chiefly manage the affair; he also consulted Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 二意相乖，時致諍競，積六載乃成，始班賜百官。

translations.literal: The two intentions diverged; at the time causing dispute and contention—accumulated six years then completed, beginning to distribute to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The two intentions diverged; at the time causing dispute and contention—accumulated six years then completed, beginning to distribute to the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 冠服之成，少游有效焉。

translations.literal: When robes and caps were completed, Shaoyou had effect.
translations.idiomatic: When robes and caps were completed, Shaoyou had effect.

sentences.zh: 後於平城將營太廟、太極殿，遣少游乘傳詣洛，量準魏晉基趾。

translations.literal: Later at Pingcheng when about to build the Grand Temple and Grand Ultimate Hall, Shaoyou was dispatched by post-carriage to Luoyang to measure and standardize Wei and Jin foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Pingcheng when about to build the Grand Temple and Grand Ultimate Hall, Shaoyou was dispatched by post-carriage to Luoyang to measure and standardize Wei and Jin foundations.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎侍郎，副李彪使江南。

translations.literal: Later he was Regular Palace Attendant, deputy to Li Biao on mission to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Regular Palace Attendant, deputy to Li Biao on mission to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 高祖修船乘，以其多有思力，除都水使者，遷前將軍、兼將作大匠，仍領水池湖泛戲舟楫之具。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu repaired boats and carriages; because he had much thoughtful strength, he was appointed Director of Waterways, moved to General of the Vanguard and Concurrent Master of Works, still overseeing ponds, lakes, floating pleasure boats and oars.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu repaired boats and carriages; because he had much thoughtful strength, he was appointed Director of Waterways, moved to General of the Vanguard and Concurrent Master of Works, still overseeing ponds, lakes, floating pleasure boats and oars.

sentences.zh: 及華林殿、沼修舊增新，改作金墉門樓，皆所措意，號為妍美。

translations.literal: When the Hualin Hall and pond were repaired old and augmented new, altering the Golden City gate tower—all were directed by him, called refined and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hualin Hall and pond were repaired old and augmented new, altering the Golden City gate tower—all were directed by him, called refined and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 雖有文藻，而不得伸其才用，恒以剞劂繩尺，碎劇怱怱，徙倚園湖城殿之側，識者為之歎慨。

translations.literal: Though he had literary ornament, he could not extend his talent and use; constantly with carving, compass, and ruler, trivial and hurried, lingering beside the garden ponds and city halls—knowers sighed for him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had literary ornament, he could not extend his talent and use; constantly with carving, compass, and ruler, trivial and hurried, lingering beside the garden ponds and city halls—knowers sighed for him.

sentences.zh: 而乃坦爾為己任，不告疲耻。

translations.literal: Yet he calmly took it as his own task, not reporting fatigue or shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he calmly took it as his own task, not reporting fatigue or shame.

sentences.zh: 又兼太常少卿，都水如故。

translations.literal: He was also Concurrent Vice Minister of Ceremonies, Director of Waterways as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was also Concurrent Vice Minister of Ceremonies, Director of Waterways as before.

sentences.zh: 景明二年卒，贈龍驤將軍、青州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: He died in Jingming 2; posthumously granted General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Qingzhou, posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingming 2; posthumously granted General of Flying Dragons and Governor of Qingzhou, posthumous title Zhi.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷餘。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings of more than ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected writings of more than ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 少游又為太極立模範，與董尒、王遇等參建之，皆未成而卒。

translations.literal: Shaoyou also made models for the Grand Ultimate, together with Dong Er, Wang Yu, and others jointly building them—all not completed before death.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou also made models for the Grand Ultimate, together with Dong Er, Wang Yu, and others jointly building them—all not completed before death.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗時，郭善明甚機巧，北京宮殿，多其製作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's time, Guo Shanming was very ingenious; the northern capital's palaces and halls were mostly his production.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's time, Guo Shanming was very ingenious; the northern capital's palaces and halls were mostly his production.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，青州刺史侯文和亦以巧聞，為要舟，水中立射。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time, Inspector of Qingzhou Hou Wenhe was also known for cleverness; he made essential boats, standing to shoot in water.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozu's time, Inspector of Qingzhou Hou Wenhe was also known for cleverness; he made essential boats, standing to shoot in water.

sentences.zh: 滑稽多智，辭說無端，尤善淺俗委巷之語，至可玩笑。

translations.literal: Humorous and witty, very clever in speech, speaking without end, especially skilled in shallow vulgar alley language—most fit for jest.
translations.idiomatic: Humorous and witty, very clever in speech, speaking without end, especially skilled in shallow vulgar alley language—most fit for jest.

sentences.zh: 位樂陵、濟南二郡太守。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Administrator of Leling and Jinan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Administrator of Leling and Jinan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 世宗、肅宗時，豫州人柳儉、殿中將軍關文備、郭安興並機巧。

translations.literal: In the times of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Suzong, Liu Jian of Yuzhou, Palace Guard General Guan Wenbei, and Guo Anxing of the palace were all ingenious.
translations.idiomatic: In the times of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Suzong, Liu Jian of Yuzhou, Palace Guard General Guan Wenbei, and Guo Anxing of the palace were all ingenious.

sentences.zh: 洛中製永寧寺九層佛圖，安興為匠也。

translations.literal: In Luoyang they made the nine-story Buddhist pagoda of Yongning Temple; Anxing was the craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang they made the nine-story Buddhist pagoda of Yongning Temple; Anxing was the craftsman.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，有范寧兒者善圍碁。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time there was Fan Ning'er skilled at weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozu's time there was Fan Ning'er skilled at weiqi.

sentences.zh: 曾與李彪使蕭賾，賾令江南上品王抗與寧兒。

translations.literal: Once with Li Biao he was envoy to Xiao Ze; Ze ordered Jiangnan's highest-grade Wang Kang to play with Ning'er.
translations.idiomatic: Once with Li Biao he was envoy to Xiao Ze; Ze ordered Jiangnan's highest-grade Wang Kang to play with Ning'er.

sentences.zh: [16]制勝而還。

translations.literal: [16] Victorious and returned.
translations.idiomatic: [16] Victorious and returned.

sentences.zh: 又有浮陽高光宗善樗蒲。

translations.literal: Also there was Gaoguang Zong of Fuyang skilled at chupu.
translations.idiomatic: Also there was Gaoguang Zong of Fuyang skilled at chupu.

sentences.zh: 趙國李幼序、洛陽丘何奴並工握槊。

translations.literal: Li Youxu of Zhao kingdom and Qiu Henu of Luoyang were both skilled at woro.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youxu of Zhao kingdom and Qiu Henu of Luoyang were both skilled at woro.

sentences.zh: 此蓋胡戲，近入中國，云胡王有弟一人遇罪，將殺之，弟從獄中為此戲以上之，意言孤則易死也。

translations.literal: This is roughly a barbarian game, recently entering China—it is said the barbarian king had a younger brother who met punishment and was about to be killed; the younger brother from prison made this game to present upward—the meaning saying "alone then easily dies."
translations.idiomatic: This is roughly a barbarian game, recently entering China—it is said the barbarian king had a younger brother who met punishment and was about to be killed; the younger brother from prison made this game to present upward—the meaning saying "alone then easily dies."

sentences.zh: 世宗以後，大盛於時。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shizong it greatly flourished at the time.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizong it greatly flourished at the time.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陰陽卜祝之事，聖哲之教存焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Matters of yin-yang divination and prayer—the teaching of sages exists therein.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Matters of yin-yang divination and prayer—the teaching of sages exists therein.

sentences.zh: 雖不可以專，亦不可得而廢也。

translations.literal: Though one cannot specialize in them, one also cannot abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Though one cannot specialize in them, one also cannot abolish them.

sentences.zh: 徇於是者不能無非，厚於利者必有其害。

translations.literal: Those who pursue them cannot be without fault; those thick in profit must have harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pursue them cannot be without fault; those thick in profit must have harm.

sentences.zh: 詩書禮樂，所失也鮮，故先王重其德；

translations.literal: Poetry, documents, rites, and music—what is lost is slight; thus former kings weighted their virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Poetry, documents, rites, and music—what is lost is slight; thus former kings weighted their virtue;

sentences.zh: 方術伎巧，所失也深，故往哲輕其藝。

translations.literal: methods and arts, skill and cleverness—what is lost is deep; thus former sages lightened their crafts.
translations.idiomatic: methods and arts, skill and cleverness—what is lost is deep; thus former sages lightened their crafts.

sentences.zh: 夫能通方術而不詭於俗，習伎巧而必蹈於禮者，幾于大雅君子。

translations.literal: One who can master methods and arts without being deceptive toward the vulgar, practice skill and cleverness yet must tread in ritual—nearly a great-standard gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: One who can master methods and arts without being deceptive toward the vulgar, practice skill and cleverness yet must tread in ritual—nearly a great-standard gentleman.

sentences.zh: 故昔之通賢，所以戒乎妄作。

translations.literal: Thus the sages of old therefore warned against reckless action.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sages of old therefore warned against reckless action.

sentences.zh: 晁崇、張淵、王早、殷紹、耿玄、劉靈助皆術藝之士也。

translations.literal: Chao Chong, Zhang Yuan, Wang Zao, Yin Shao, Geng Xuan, and Liu Lingzhu were all men of methods and arts.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Chong, Zhang Yuan, Wang Zao, Yin Shao, Geng Xuan, and Liu Lingzhu were all men of methods and arts.

sentences.zh: 觀其占候卜筮，推步盈虛，通幽洞微，近知鬼神之情狀。

translations.literal: Observing their observation and prognostication, divination by tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, calculating steps of surplus and insufficiency, penetrating the obscure and subtle—they nearly know the sentiments and forms of ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Observing their observation and prognostication, divination by tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, calculating steps of surplus and insufficiency, penetrating the obscure and subtle—they nearly know the sentiments and forms of ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 周澹、李脩、徐謇、王顯、崔彧方藥特妙，各一時之美也。

translations.literal: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu Jian, Wang Xian, and Cui Yu—medicinal formulas especially marvelous, each the beauty of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu Jian, Wang Xian, and Cui Yu—medicinal formulas especially marvelous, each the beauty of an age.

sentences.zh: 蔣少游以剞劂見知，沒其學思，藝成為下，其近是乎？

translations.literal: Jiang Shaoyou was known for carving—his learning and thought submerged, craft completed yet inferior—is this not close?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shaoyou was known for carving—his learning and thought submerged, craft completed yet inferior—is this not close?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 蔣少游 按卷七下高祖紀太和十五年十一月乙亥條、卷五九劉昶傳、卷六八高聰傳「游」並作「遊」。

translations.literal: Jiang Shaoyou: According to the entry for the yihai day of the eleventh month of the fifteenth year of Taihe in juan 7B Gaozu benji, juan 59 Liu Chang zhuan, and juan 68 Gao Cong zhuan, "游" is all written as "遊."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shaoyou: According to the entry for the yihai day of the eleventh month of the fifteenth year of Taihe in juan 7B Gaozu benji, juan 59 Liu Chang zhuan, and juan 68 Gao Cong zhuan, "游" is all written as "遊."

sentences.zh: 北史此二傳「遊」「游」雜出。

translations.literal: In Beishi these two biographies have "遊" and "游" mixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Beishi these two biographies have "遊" and "游" mixed.

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五七魏虜傳作「游」。

translations.literal: Nanjie shu juan 57 Wei lu zhuan writes "游."
translations.idiomatic: Nanjie shu juan 57 Wei lu zhuan writes "游."

sentences.zh: 當時名字本通用同音字。

translations.literal: At the time personal names originally universally used homophonic characters.
translations.idiomatic: At the time personal names originally universally used homophonic characters.

sentences.zh: 此傳出於北史，北史卷九０下作「游」，今皆仍之。

translations.literal: This biography comes from Beishi; Beishi juan 90B writes "游"—now all follow it.
translations.idiomatic: This biography comes from Beishi; Beishi juan 90B writes "游"—now all follow it.

sentences.zh: 魏書卷九十一 諸本目錄注「不全」，卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: Weishu juan 91: Various editions' table of contents notes "incomplete"; at the end of the scroll is a Song-dynasty collation note
translations.idiomatic: Weishu juan 91: Various editions' tables of contents note "incomplete"; at the scroll's end is a Song-dynasty collation note.

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Dianben entered Kaozheng〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Palace edition entered textual verification〉

sentences.zh: 云：「此卷王顯以前魏收舊書，崔彧、蔣少游傳全出北史及小史，史臣論亦全出北史藝術傳論，而北史全用周、隋書藝術傳論云。」

translations.literal: It says: "Before Wang Xian in this scroll is Wei Shou's old book; the biographies of Cui Yu and Jiang Shaoyou entirely come from Beishi and Xiaoshi, and the historian's discussion also entirely comes from Beishi's Yishu zhuan lun—and Beishi entirely uses the Zhou and Sui shu Yishu zhuan lun."
translations.idiomatic: It states: "Before Wang Xian this scroll preserves Wei Shou's original text; the biographies of Cui Yu and Jiang Shaoyou are wholly drawn from Beishi and Xiaoshi, and the historian's discussion likewise comes from Beishi's Arts biography discussion—and Beishi in turn draws entirely on the Zhou and Sui shu Arts biography discussions."

sentences.zh: 黃帝靈威仰位東方 按東方青帝靈威仰，見周禮天官太宰祀五帝條疏。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor Lingweiyang in the east: According to the commentary on the Grand Steward sacrificing to the Five Emperors in Zhouli tianguan taizai.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Emperor Lingweiyang in the east: per the commentary on the Grand Steward's sacrifice to the Five Emperors in the Rites of Zhou, Heavenly Offices, Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 且下文又見「黃帝含樞紐在中央」，這裏「黃帝」當是「青帝」之訛。

translations.literal: And below also appears "Yellow Emperor Hanshuniu in the center"—here "Yellow Emperor" should be the error for "Green Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Below also appears "Yellow Emperor Hanshuniu in the center"—here "Yellow Emperor" is likely an error for "Green Emperor."

sentences.zh: 案天占以言災異 北史卷八九張淵附孫僧化傳「天」作「文」。

translations.literal: Examining celestial prognostication to speak of disasters and anomalies: Beishi juan 89 Zhang Yuan fu Sun Seng hua zhuan writes "天" as "文."
translations.idiomatic: On examining celestial prognostication to discuss disasters and anomalies: Beishi juan 89, Zhang Yuan appendix Sun Seng hua zhuan, writes "天" as "文."

sentences.zh: 疑當作「天文占」。

translations.literal: Suspected should read "天文占."
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected the text should read "天文占" (celestial prognostication).

sentences.zh: 隋書卷三四經籍志子部天文類著錄天文集占、天文占、天文橫占、天文外官占等書可證，此傳及北史各脫一字。

translations.literal: Suishu juan 34 Jingji zhi zibu tianwen lei records Celestial Prognostication Collection, Celestial Prognostication, Celestial Prognostication Horizontal, Celestial Prognostication Outer Official, and other books can verify—this biography and Beishi each drop one character.
translations.idiomatic: Suishu juan 34, Bibliographic Treatise, Masters section, Astronomy category, lists Celestial Prognostication Collection, Celestial Prognostication, Celestial Prognostication Horizontal, Celestial Prognostication Outer Official, and similar works as evidence—this biography and Beishi each omit one character.

sentences.zh: 字王琳 北史卷八九信都芳傳「王」作「玉」，疑是。

translations.literal: Courtesy name Wang Lin: Beishi juan 89 Xindu Fang zhuan writes "王" as "玉"—suspected correct.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy name Wang Lin: Beishi juan 89, Xindu Fang zhuan, writes "王" as "玉"—likely correct.

sentences.zh: 又史遷郝振中古大儒 諸本「古」訛「吉」，今據冊府卷八六九

translations.literal: Also Shi Qian and Hao Zhen, great scholars of middle antiquity: Various editions err "古" as "吉"—now according to Cefu juan 869
translations.idiomatic: Also on Shi Qian and Hao Zhen, great scholars of middle antiquity: various editions wrongly write "古" as "吉"—corrected now according to Cefu juan 869

sentences.zh: 〈一０三一０頁〉
改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 明陰陽九宮及兵法 諸本「宮」作「官」，北史卷八九作「宮」。

translations.literal: Understood yin-yang, Nine Palaces, and military arts: Various editions write "宮" as "官"; Beishi juan 89 writes "宮."
translations.idiomatic: On "understood yin-yang, Nine Palaces, and military arts": various editions write "宮" as "官"; Beishi juan 89 has "宮."

sentences.zh: 按後漢書卷五九張衡傳，衡上疏有云「重之以卜筮，雜之以九宮」。

translations.literal: According to Hou Hanshu juan 59 Zhang Heng zhuan, Heng's memorial says "additionally with divination by tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, mixed with the Nine Palaces."
translations.idiomatic: According to Hou Hanshu juan 59, Zhang Heng zhuan, Heng's memorial says "additionally with divination by tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, mixed with the Nine Palaces."

sentences.zh: 九宮是一種占卜術，隋書卷三四經籍志子部五行類著錄以「九宮」為名的黃帝九宮經等書多種。

translations.literal: Nine Palaces is a type of divination art; Suishu juan 34 Jingji zhi zibu wuxing lei records many books with "Nine Palaces" in the title such as Yellow Emperor Nine Palaces Classic.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Palaces is a form of divination; Suishu juan 34, Bibliographic Treatise, Masters section, Five Agents category, records many works titled with "Nine Palaces," such as the Yellow Emperor Nine Palaces Classic.

sentences.zh: 「官」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "官" is erroneous—now corrected according to evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The character "官" is erroneous and is corrected here according to the evidence.

sentences.zh: 而齊獻武王以明年閏二月破四胡於韓陵山 諸本「四」作「西」。

translations.literal: While Prince Xianwu of Qi in the intercalary second month of the following year broke the Four Hu at Hanling Mountain: Various editions write "四" as "西."
translations.idiomatic: On "while Prince Xianwu of Qi in the intercalary second month of the following year broke the Four Hu at Hanling Mountain": various editions write "四" as "西."

sentences.zh: 按四胡屢見紀傳，指尒朱兆、天光、度律、仲遠四人，卷一一後廢帝紀中興二年閏三月壬戌稱「齊獻武王大破尒朱天光等四胡於韓陵」。

translations.literal: According to Four Hu repeatedly appearing in annals and biographies, referring to the four men Erzhu Zhao, Tian Guang, Dulu, and Zhongyuan; juan 11 Houfeidi benji Zhongxing 2 intercalary third month renchen says "Prince Xianwu of Qi greatly broke Erzhu Tian Guang and the others, the Four Hu, at Hanling."
translations.idiomatic: The Four Hu appear repeatedly in annals and biographies, referring to Erzhu Zhao, Tian Guang, Dulu, and Zhongyuan; juan 11, Houfeidi benji, Zhongxing 2, intercalary third month renchen says "Prince Xianwu of Qi greatly broke Erzhu Tian Guang and the others, the Four Hu, at Hanling."

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now corrected according to evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here according to the evidence.

sentences.zh: 又「閏二月」亦是「閏三月」之訛。

translations.literal: Also "intercalary second month" is also the error for "intercalary third month."
translations.idiomatic: Also, "intercalary second month" is likely an error for "intercalary third month."

sentences.zh: 古今字詁 三朝本、南本、汲本、局本「詁」作「訓」，北本、殿本及北史卷三四江式傳作「詁」。

translations.literal: Ancient-and-Modern Character Glosses: Sanchao ben, Nan ben, Ji ben, Ju ben write "詁" as "訓"; Bei ben, Dian ben, and Beishi juan 34 Jiang Shi zhuan write "詁."
translations.idiomatic: Ancient-and-Modern Character Glosses: Sanchao ben, Nan ben, Ji ben, and Ju ben write "詁" as "訓"; Bei ben, Dian ben, and Beishi juan 34, Jiang Shi zhuan, have "詁."

sentences.zh: 按下文兩稱「古今字詁」，隋書卷三二經籍志經部小學類同。

translations.literal: According to below twice calling it "Ancient-and-Modern Character Glosses," Suishu juan 32 Jingji zhi jingbu xiaoxue lei same.
translations.idiomatic: The text below twice calls it "Ancient-and-Modern Character Glosses," matching Suishu juan 32, Bibliographic Treatise, Classics section, Philology category.

sentences.zh: 今從北、殿本。

translations.literal: Now follow Bei and Dian editions.
translations.idiomatic: The Bei and Dian editions are followed here.

translations.literal: Broad in antiquity and opening arts: Beishi juan 34 Jiang Shi zhuan this phrase has "古开" reversed; Cefu juan 608
translations.idiomatic: On "broad in antiquity and opening arts": Beishi juan 34, Jiang Shi zhuan, reverses "古开" in this phrase; Cefu juan 608

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 7294〉

translations.literal: Writes "博聞古藝"—suspected correct.
translations.idiomatic: has "博聞古藝"—likely correct.

translations.idiomatic: On "small rabbit" for snow: various editions write "兔" as "兒"; Beishi juan 34 and Cefu

translations.literal: 〈Same juan page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same fascicle, same page〉

translations.idiomatic: have "兔."

translations.literal: According to Guangyun juan 19 Hou, "䨲, rabbit," thus vulgarly written "small rabbit"—the character "兒" is erroneous; now corrected according to evidence.
translations.idiomatic: According to Guangyun juan 19 Hou, "䨲 means rabbit," hence the vulgar form "small rabbit"—the character "兒" is erroneous and is corrected here according to the evidence.

translations.literal: Zuwenzong: According to this book not seen in preceding text, also not seen in Suishu Jingji zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zuwenzong: this work is not mentioned in the preceding text and does not appear in the Suishu Bibliographic Treatise.

translations.idiomatic: Cefu juan 859

translations.idiomatic: reads "Formerly when Jin Emperor Wu had sudden illness, Cheng He advanced drugs, increased enfeoffment and granted cash, grace and reward repeatedly arriving"—suspected to be an intentional alteration.

sentences.zh: 少與李亮同師 諸本「李」作「季」，北史卷九０王顯傳作「李」。

translations.literal: In youth studied under the same teacher as Li Liang: Various editions write "李" as "季"; Beishi juan 90 Wang Xian zhuan writes "李."
translations.idiomatic: On "in youth studied under the same teacher as Li Liang": various editions write "李" as "季"; Beishi juan 90, Wang Xian zhuan, has "李."

sentences.zh: 按李亮見前李脩傳。

translations.literal: According to Li Liang seen in preceding Li Xiu zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang appears in the preceding Li Xiu zhuan.

sentences.zh: 「季」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "季" is erroneous—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The character "季" is erroneous and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 封衞南伯 北史卷九０「衞南」作「衞國縣」。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Baron of Weinan: Beishi juan 90 writes "衞南" as "衞國縣."
translations.idiomatic: On enfeoffment as Baron of Weinan: Beishi juan 90 writes "衞南" as "衞國縣."

sentences.zh: 按卷一０六上地形志上司州頓丘郡有衞國縣，「衞南」不見地形志，疑北史是。

translations.literal: According to juan 106A Dili zhi Shang Sizhou Dunqiu jun has Weiguo county—"Weinan" not seen in Dili zhi; suspected Beishi is correct.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 106A, Dili zhi, Shang Sizhou, Dunqiu commandery, there is Weiguo county—"Weinan" does not appear in the Dili zhi; Beishi is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 賾令江南上品王抗與寧兒 張森楷云：「『兒』下當有脫文。」

translations.literal: Ze ordered Jiangnan's highest-grade Wang Kang to play with Ning'er: Zhang Senkai says: "Below 'er' there should be missing text."
translations.idiomatic: On "Ze ordered Jiangnan's highest-grade Wang Kang to play with Ning'er": Zhang Senkai says text is missing after "er."
